newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes up, market waits U.S. election.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes up, market waits U.S. election.

text.p: Gold dealers on Tuesday were looking for their market to maintain the bounce which lifted it from the lowest prices since early October struck last Friday.
But they were less sure that the recovery in the value of the metal would be smooth and steady.
"There is plenty of deadwood around. The price will be contested all the way up," said one dealer.
Gold was fixed at $379.30 per ounce, just five cents up from the morning fixing and compared to $378.70 on Monday afternoon. The recent low of $377.20 was struck on Friday morning.

"If it gets to $380.00 or $381.00 we will see it begin to struggle and a third test of $376.80 (the lowest price last month) could take it through there. It doesn't look healthy," said technical analyst Karen Jones at Credit Suisse.
Dealers said business was very slow in Europe as market participants held fire ahead of the conclusion of the U.S. presidential election.

A win for incumbent president Bill Clinton was factored into the price, dealers said. "If (Senator Bob) Dole wins there could be a reaction. But it won't be more than a dollar on the downside," one dealer said.

"Four years ago when Clinton won, Europe was dead during the morning but the New York trading session was pretty active. It wouldn't surprise me if we see some excitement this afternoon," another trader said.
Shortly after the 1500 GMT fixing there was little evidence of it with the key December futures contract on New York's Comex market up just $0.80 overnight at $380.40.
Dealers said the market's high borrowing rates of the past week were easing as borrowing subsided by gold producers against selling metal they had not yet mined.
"It looks as though there are some buy orders coming into the forward market and the producer selling has stopped for the moment," one dealer said.
Also pushing up borrowing rates was the reluctance of some central banks -- the main lenders to the market -- to enter new lending agreements so close to their year-end audit.
After lagging gold, silver was "sideways and sidelined", according to Jones. It was indicated just two cents higher than Monday at $4.83/$4.85.
Platinum and palladium were quiet and barely changed at $381.25/$382.25 and $117.25/$118.25, up $1.50 respectively.
